assertions.text: Table columns represent the method's public inputs (applicant type, age, claim count) and observable outputs (decision, premium) — not internal state like hasActivePolicy, internalRiskScore, or calculateRiskScore.
assertions.evidence: Columns are Scenario | Applicant type | Age | Claims | Decision? | Premium? — representing public inputs and observable outputs with no internal state columns present

assertions.text: No column is named after private fields or internal variables (hasActivePolicy, internalRiskScore, riskScore). The test treats the method as a black box.
assertions.evidence: Column names: Scenario, Applicant type, Age, Claims, Decision?, Premium? — none match private field names like hasActivePolicy, internalRiskScore, or riskScore

assertions.text: Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
assertions.evidence: Scenario is the first column in the table: "Scenario                    | Applicant type | Age | Claims | Decision?     | Premium?"

assertions.text: Column names use domain/business language (e.g. 'Applicant type', 'Age', 'Claims', 'Decision?', 'Premium?') — not code identifiers like 'applicantType', 'claimCount', 'String'.
assertions.evidence: Columns use business language: 'Applicant type', 'Age', 'Claims', 'Decision?', 'Premium?' rather than camelCase identifiers

assertions.text: Scenario names describe conditions ('Renewal with no claims', 'Senior applicant') — not outcomes ('Auto approved', 'Rejected').
assertions.evidence: Scenario row 'High claim count, rejected' includes 'rejected' which is an outcome word, violating the requirement that scenario names describe conditions only, not outcomes

assertions.text: Table has at least one column name ending with '?' (e.g. 'Decision?' or 'Premium?')
assertions.evidence: Table columns include 'Decision?' and 'Premium?' both ending with question marks

assertions.text: Test method body contains no if or switch statements
assertions.evidence: Method body is: 'EvaluationResult result = evaluator.evaluateApplication(applicantType, age, claimCount); assertAll(...)' with no if or switch statements

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
assertions.evidence: @DisplayName("Application evaluation") @Description(...) @TableTest(...) in that exact order before the method

assertions.text: Test method has either a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
assertions.evidence: @DisplayName("Application evaluation") provides a clear descriptive title for the test method

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: @Description uses triple-quoted text block: """\n        Risk score = (age / 10) + (claimCount × 15), integer division...\n        """ not string concatenation
